description: Connector fleet telemetry. Connection health first: a destination stuck in its unbounded redial loop and a source with no sender attached are the two failures nothing else reports.

panels.title: Longest outage now
panels.description: Seconds since anything was on the other end. Not reset by a failed redial.

panels.title: Peak redial attempts
panels.description: Attempts inside the current outage. Backoff caps at 60s, so 60 attempts is roughly an hour.

panels.title: Longest idle (connected)
panels.description: Socket open, keepalives answered, nothing arriving - the wedged-sender case.

panels.title: How long has each endpoint been down
panels.description: The clock starts when the connection drops and a failed redial does NOT reset it, so this is the series to alert on: > 300 is five minutes of real outage no matter how many attempts happened inside it. Zero means connected.

panels.title: Consecutive redial attempts
panels.description: Resets to zero on success. Because backoff widens to a 60s cap, attempts grow far more slowly than downtime - which is why both are needed.

panels.title: Endpoint up / down
panels.description: A destination dials out and self-heals. A source is a passive listener and cannot reconnect anything, so a source at 0 needs a sender or a restart.

panels.title: Live connections
panels.description: A destination holds at most one; a TCP source can hold many attached senders.

panels.title: Idle time on live connections
panels.description: Filtered to connections that are actually up. Connection age alone looks HEALTHIER the longer a sender stays wedged, which is why idle time is the signal.

panels.title: Failed dials and recoveries per minute
panels.description: Failed dials climbing with no recoveries is a dead peer. Both climbing together is a flapping link, which individual deliveries hide because each eventually succeeds.

panels.title: Stream connected, per connector
panels.description: Reported by the API from its own view of the session, so a connector that has gone away stays in place at 0 rather than vanishing - an absent series could never breach a threshold.

panels.title: Messages upstream per second, per connector
Local queue, per connector
panels.description: Messages persisted to the connector's own disk and not yet sent upstream.

panels.title: Configured vs running protocols, per connector
panels.description: A gap means a protocol died after starting. One that never started is absent from both counts.

panels.title: Utilization per connector — alert on the ratio, debug on the absolutes
panels.description: A missing line means the denominator was unavailable, which is different from a line at zero. The queue, connection count and sync cache are unbounded, so they appear as absolutes only.

panels.title: Process memory and open descriptors
panels.description: RSS matters because the connector buffers whole message bodies while splitting a batch. Descriptors sit on their own axis against their rlimit.
